description: Citrus greening is one of the most destructive diseases of citrus trees. It is caused by bacteria of the genus Liberibacter and transmitted mainly by psyllid insects. Infected trees produce small, bitter, poorly colored fruits and eventually decline and die within a few years. There is currently no cure for the disease.
symptoms_and_damage: Yellowing of leaf veins and shoots
Twig dieback and premature leaf drop
Fruits remain partly green when ripe
Aborted seeds and poor fruit development
disease_cycle_and_spread: Bacteria live in the phloem tissue of citrus trees
Spread mainly by psyllid insects feeding on infected plants
Can also spread through grafting infected plant material
Young psyllid stages acquire the bacteria and transmit it to healthy plants
favorable_conditions: Warm climates in tropical and subtropical regions
distribution: United States (Florida, Texas, California and others)
Many tropical and subtropical citrus-growing regions worldwide
management: Use clean and certified planting material
notes: Infected trees usually die within a few years
The disease has caused major economic losses in citrus industries worldwide
sources: USDA – Citrus Greening and Asian Citrus Psyllid
